title: Dvořák's conjecture on coloring squares of girth-five planar graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph with girth $5$, let $\Delta$ denote its maximum degree, and let $M$ be a constant. The **Dvořák conjecture.** There exists some constant $M$ such that every planar graph $G$ with girth $5$ and maximum degree at least $M$ satisfies

$$
\Delta(G^2)\le\Delta+2.
$$

Here $G^2$ is the square of $G$ and $\Delta(G^2)$ denotes its maximum degree. This conjecture concerns the remaining high-degree, girth-five case after known results for larger girth; the supplied text gives no resolution, so it is open.
source_name: Daniel W. Cranston and Bobby Jaeger, “List-coloring the Squares of Planar Graphs without 4-Cycles and 5-Cycles”, arXiv:1505.03197 (2015).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.03197

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2015). “Although the conjecture remains open in general, Havet et al.\ showed that the conjectured upper bound holds asymptotically, i.e., $\chi(G^2) \le \frac{3}{2}\Delta + o(\Delta)$.”
